extracted.intended_audience: patent prosecutors (patent attorneys, agents), in-house counsel, and applicants evaluating USPTO examiner behavior during prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on using examiner-level USPTO statistics to inform prosecution choices (amendments, interviews, appeals), including what metrics to inspect and how to apply them to strategy and client counseling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment information
rubrics_metrics.description: See your examiner's education level, their location, and how long they've been at the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use biographical/employment details to contextualize examiner behavior (e.g., experience level may correlate with grant/difficulty patterns). No explicit examples given on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant rate and difficulty rating
rubrics_metrics.description: See how hard your examiner is compared to other examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare an examiner's grant rate and an aggregated difficulty score to peers to judge likelihood of allowance. Use this to set expectations and guide decisions like interviewing or amending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant rate timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: See our predictions for how long it will take to get your patent allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the timeline predictions to estimate prosecution duration. Use projected time-to-allow when advising clients about cost, timing, or whether to pursue appeal versus continued prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn if requesting an interview will help or hurt your case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at historical interview outcomes for the examiner to decide whether requesting an interview is likely to be beneficial. Use this to decide whether to request or prepare differently for interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recent dispositions (free)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read about past dispositions that were abandoned and approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine recent dispositions to see concrete past outcomes (abandonments, approvals) as context for likely results. Free tier provides disposition summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recent dispositions with office-action rejections (premium)
rubrics_metrics.description: See the rejections (e.g., 101, 102, and 103) made in individual office actions to find relevant arguments made by other attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use detailed recent office actions to find the specific rejection types and arguments an examiner applies; use those examples as precedent for drafting responses or anticipating examiner positions. This feature is part of the premium tier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Share appeals statistics with clients to help them make better-informed decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use aggregated appeals metrics to quantify historical appeal outcomes for the examiner or art unit when counseling clients on whether to appeal. Can support cost/benefit analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals history
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the appeal history of an examiner to determine whether or not you should appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate individual examiner appeal records (e.g., frequency, success rates) to decide whether an appeal is strategically warranted for a given file. Premium features surface this history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictions of appeal success and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Our predictions of appeal success and outcomes help you make better decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on predicted appeal success probabilities and outcome estimates to weigh the expected value of appealing versus other routes (amendment, continued prosecution). Use predictions as one input among legal analysis and client goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant rate by role/assignment (example: Examiner P/S and art unit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per-art-unit and per-examiner grant-rate snapshots (e.g., 'In Art Unit 2628: 1% Examiner P grant rate; 93% Examiner S grant rate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine grant rates at the art-unit or examiner-role level to see intra-art-unit variation and whether specific examiner roles favor allowance or rejection. Use this to set expectations and tailor tactics to the assigned examiner/role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use stats to decide whether to amend claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't amend your claims unless you need to. Make better decisions about when and how to amend claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner historically allows broader claims or benefits from interviews/arguments, avoid unnecessary narrowing amendments. Use rejection patterns and allowance likelihood to decide whether to amend and how narrowly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use stats to prepare for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Know your examiner before going into an interview. Adjust your strategy based on the difficulty of the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult interview benefit metrics and examiner difficulty to plan whether to request an interview, who should attend, and what arguments or claim sets to present. Historical behavior informs optimal interview tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use stats to make better appeal decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals are long and expensive. Our predictions of appeal success and outcomes help you make better decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine appeals statistics, appeal-history details, and predicted outcomes to determine whether to appeal a rejection. Use these metrics to counsel clients on expected costs and success probabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set client expectations with hard data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use hard data to let your client know what you are up against and to support your prosecution recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present examiner-specific metrics (grant rates, timelines, appeal history) to clients to justify strategy recommendations and manage expectations about scope, timing, and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium vs Free feature availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Free Statistics are available to all logged-in users; Premium Statistics require a paid subscription.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know which metrics are accessible without subscription (employment info, basic grant rates, timelines, interview benefit, recent dispositions) versus which require premium (detailed office-action rejections, appeals history/statistics). Use tier availability when planning research workflow or budget for analytics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use statistics to obtain broader patents / minimize unnecessary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain broader patents — Don't amend your claims unless you need to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When examiner statistics indicate an allowance trend or receptivity to arguments, favor arguing rather than narrowing claims to preserve claim breadth. Use historical rejection types and allowance pathways to craft arguments that preserve scope.
